description: Implementation of the Project for the safe and climate-resilient water supply for the cities in the Western Province
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-03-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The impact of climate change is severely affecting the supply of safe drinking water in many parts of Sri Lanka. There is a pressing need to build resilience against weather conditions such as floods and droughts through climate-resilient water supply plans as an essential component of water supply management. The project proposal “safe and climate-change-resilient water supply for cities in the Western Province: Integration of Climate-Change-Resilience Concepts into the Water Safety Plan of the Ambatale Water Supply Scheme” has been submitted by the Environmental and Social Division which is established by the National Water Supply and Drainage Board, to be responsive to gender equality, including ensuring environmental sustainability and social accountability, and strengthening resilience to climate and disaster risks, as a response for request for proposals made by the  ‘Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure’, based on the advice of UN Habitat. Accordingly, a financial grant of US$ 469,232 has been received to implement the proposed project within a period of 24 months. The National Water Supply and Drainage Board will provide financial assistance for the project through a co-financing of US$ 10,000. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Housing, Construction and Water Supply for the implementation of the proposed project, was approved by the Cabinet.
